channel.title: Simulatio Lab | New experiments
channel.description: New experiments from the lab that reruns the world

item.title: Why Does My Bond Fall When Rates Rise? The 10-Year Treasury Yield
item.description: See how short-rate paths set the 10-year yield and how much a bond you already hold falls when rates rise one point. (Example numbers, not a forecast.)

item.title: Buying the High-Rate Currency: The Carry Trade That Takes the Stairs Up and the Elevator Down
item.description: Holding a higher-yield currency can earn a little for years and lose a lot at once. See the shape crowding and unwinding create. (Example numbers, not investment advice.)

item.title: How Many Should You Meet Before Choosing? The 37% Rule
item.description: When you cannot go back, how much should you watch before choosing to have the best chance at the very best? Check the famous 37% answer yourself.

item.title: Why Do Job Tips Come from Acquaintances, Not Close Friends? The Strength of Weak Ties
item.description: Tie just a few acquaintances into tight friend circles and news spreads several times faster.

item.title: Why Is One Shared Checkout Line Faster?
item.description: Same cashiers, same customers: one shared line or many separate ones changes both waiting time and fairness.

item.title: Why Do Buses Always Come in Pairs?
item.description: Why do evenly spaced buses end up in clumps? Run the feedback where more passengers means more delay, and test remedies.

item.title: How Many Strangers Can Fit on a Bench?
item.description: Everyone sat politely apart, yet seats go unused. Compare four ways of sitting side by side to see why.

item.title: Why Do Lightning, Coral and Frost Look Alike?
item.description: A rule as simple as "stick on touch" grows branching shapes like lightning and coral. Change the stickiness and grow your own.

item.title: Can a Single Grain of Sand Cause a Landslide?
item.description: Adding sand one grain at a time, the pile organizes itself to a critical state: mostly quiet, now and then a huge avalanche.

item.title: Why Putting Out Every Small Fire Can Lead to Bigger Ones Later
item.description: See how putting out small fires lets fuel pile up and big fires multiply, with two forests running side by side.

item.title: A Two-Rule Ant Suddenly Builds a Road After 10,000 Steps: Langton's Ant
item.description: An ant with just two rules makes symmetry, then chaos, then suddenly a diagonal road after about 10,000 steps.

item.title: How Did Farming Cross a Continent? About One Kilometer a Year
item.description: Population growth plus a little dispersal is enough for farming to cover the land at about a kilometer a year. Watch it on a map.

item.title: Why Double the Soldiers Is Four Times as Strong: Why Splitting Up Loses
item.description: Twice the numbers means four times the strength. See the square law and why splitting your force loses, with two armies wearing each other down.

item.title: Nobody Wants It, Yet War Happens: Failed Bargains, Arms Races, and Spreading
item.description: War costs both sides, so why does it happen? Run failed bargaining, arms races and spreading among nameless abstract states. (It does not explain any real war.)

item.title: Why Does Everyone Adding One More Class Move Nobody Up?
item.description: One family alone climbs, but when all do it only the bill grows. Compare relative and absolute grading. (Example numbers, no advice.)

item.title: Why Do Kids Keep Getting Sick at Daycare? Class Size and Staying Home
item.description: See how class size, staying home when sick and built-up immunity change the colds in a year. (Reference model only.)

item.title: Who Gets the Seat? First-Come, Lottery or Preference-Based Matching
item.description: Does misreporting your ranking pay? Run four matching methods side by side. (Not the real admission system.)

item.title: A New Road Made Everyone Slower
item.description: Open a shortcut and everyone's commute gets longer? Let drivers pick their own routes and see.

item.title: Praise Them and They Slip, Scold Them and They Improve
item.description: Even if words do nothing, scolding seems to work and praise seems to backfire. What does the coach learn?

item.title: Bullet Holes on Returning Planes: Where Does the Armor Go?
item.description: The places with no holes may be the real weak spots. Add the planes that never came back.

item.title: Why Do My Friends Have More Friends Than I Do?
item.description: Popular people appear on many friend lists. Click a person to check.

item.title: Why Does the Bus Always Make You Wait Longer?
item.description: If a bus comes every 10 minutes on average, how long do you wait on average? It is also why your class always seems crowded.

item.title: A Coincidence That Isn't a Coincidence?
item.description: With 23 people, there's a 50% chance that two share a birthday. But how different is the chance that someone shares yours?

item.title: Is Success Talent or Luck?
item.description: Talent clusters around the average, so why does wealth pile up in a few hands? Is the richest person really the most talented?

item.title: Wealth Concentration
item.description: Even if every trade is as fair as a coin flip, does wealth concentrate? How much sharing does it take to stop it?

item.title: Why Do Only the Top 1% of YouTubers Break Through?
item.description: Does good content win, or do channels that broke out first keep winning? Compare parallel universes that start with the same channels.

item.title: Why Does Winning an Auction Cost You?
item.description: The highest bidder wins, so why does the winner lose on average? How much should you shade your bid to break even?

item.title: How Do Apartment Prices Spread?
item.description: See, in a toy model, how a rise in one neighborhood spreads to the next, and what lending limits and interest rates do.

item.title: Why Birds of a Feather Flock Together
item.description: Can a mild wish like "I don't want to be a minority" split a neighborhood completely apart?

item.title: Rumor Spread in Group Chats
item.description: How fast does a rumor spread, and through whom? How late can a correction come and still matter?

item.title: Does Lowering Your Standards Help You Find a Match?
item.description: See how aspiration level affects the time to find a partner in a market where both sides must agree.

item.title: Why Do Incompetent Bosses Exist?
item.description: Does promoting your best performers make an organization better? Compare promotion methods.

item.title: Does the Voting Method Change the Winner?
item.description: Count the same votes by plurality, runoff, ranked-choice and Borda. Can the winner change?

item.title: Phantom Traffic Jams: Why Does Traffic Stop Without an Accident?
item.description: Watch how one occasional tap on the brakes can jam a whole road.

item.title: Why Is the Popular Restaurant Always Packed?
item.description: Why does everyone lose when everyone thinks alike? And what if predictions differ?

item.title: What Happens When Queue-Jumping Spreads?
item.description: Test the idea that order isn't kept by itself but by someone paying a price to keep it.

item.title: Why Do Fireflies Flash in Unison?
item.description: Watch hundreds of fireflies fall into the same rhythm with no conductor.

item.title: How Does a Zebra Get Its Stripes?
item.description: Two simple reacting chemicals can form spots, stripes and mazes by themselves. Drop your own seeds.

item.title: How Does a Revolution Begin?
item.description: When everyone has a different "I'll join if this many others do" threshold, can one person change the whole square?

item.title: Why Did Easter Island Collapse?
item.description: Forest and people grow together, then crash: trace the overshoot-and-collapse curve. (The real history is still debated.)

item.title: How Does a Single Shot Become a World War?
item.description: How far does a small clash spread as alliances get denser? A cascade experiment with anonymous states.

item.title: Do Nice People Survive?
item.description: In a world full of defectors, how do cooperation and trust come back? What changes when mistakes creep in?

item.title: Which Society Would You Choose Behind the Veil of Ignorance?
item.description: If you didn't know who you'd be, which society would you pick? The choice flips with how much you dislike risk.

item.title: Is the Tragedy of the Commons Inevitable?
item.description: Is a shared pasture doomed, or can monitoring and rules save it? Run both views side by side.

item.title: Can Monkeys Write Hamlet?
item.description: Compare monkeys typing at random with evolution that keeps the best at every step.

item.title: Why Are a Few Words Used Constantly?
item.description: Why do a few words make up most of any text? Generate one yourself with a rich-get-richer rule.

item.title: How Do Stories Change as They're Retold?
item.description: What survives as a story passes from mouth to mouth? Watch as only the memorable parts remain.

item.title: Why Does Fashion Go in Cycles?
item.description: On a color wheel, watch the cycle created by a copying crowd and trendsetters running away.

item.title: What If 100 AI Painters Copy Each Other?
item.description: Does imitation collapse styles into one? Watch 100 paintings change.

item.title: Why Do Sunflower Seeds Sit at That Angle?
item.description: Turn each seed by 137.5° and they pack with no gaps. Nudge the angle and watch the pattern fall apart.

item.title: What If Korea's Birth Rate Stays This Low Until 2070?
item.description: If fertility stays as it is, how does the population pyramid change? Try other fertility and migration levels.
